definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese form of comedic storytelling performed by a single seated performer using only a fan and a small cloth as props.

examples.japanese: {落語|らくご}を{聞|き}きに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to listen to rakugo.

examples.japanese: {落語|らくご}の{オチ|おち}が{面白|おもしろ}かった。
examples.english: The punchline of the rakugo was funny.

examples.japanese: {落語|らくご}{家|か}になるには{長|なが}い{修行|しゅぎょう}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
examples.english: Becoming a rakugo performer requires long training.

notes:
COMPOUND: {落|らく} (fall, drop) + {語|ご} (words, story) - referring to the "落ち" (punchline/fall)

PERFORMANCE STYLE:
・Performed seated on a cushion ({座布団|ざぶとん})
・Uses only two props: a fan ({扇子|せんす}) and a small cloth ({手拭|てぬぐい})
・One performer plays all characters, using voice and posture changes

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{落語|らくご}を{聞|き}く (to listen to rakugo)
・{落語|らくご}{家|か} (rakugo performer)
・{寄席|よせ} (rakugo theater/variety hall)
・{オチ|おち}/{落|お}ち (punchline)
・{古典|こてん}{落語|らくご} (classical rakugo)
・{新作|しんさく}{落語|らくご} (new/modern rakugo)

FAMOUS VENUES:
・{鈴本|すずもと}{演芸場|えんげいじょう} (Suzumoto Engei Hall - Tokyo)
・{天満|てんま}{天神繁昌亭|てんじんはんじょうてい} (Osaka)
